summary: Cleburne County, AL steel lookout tower in the Talladega National Forest; a 1941 survey description is the only dated source, and none says if it still stands.

facts.status_note: No source we found says whether the tower still stands.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey described the tower and its survey station; the datasheet gives no build date

evidence.supports: described by the Coast and Geodetic Survey in 1941
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1941 (GWL)

evidence.supports: four-legged steel structure about 125 feet tall
evidence.quote: TOWER IS A FOUR-LEGGED STEEL STRUCTURE ABOUT 125 FEET IN HEIGHT

evidence.supports: winding stairway up the center of the tower
evidence.quote: A WINDING STAIRWAY LEADS UP THROUGH THE CENTER OF
THE TOWER TO THE GLASS ENCLOSED LOOKOUT IN THE TOP OF THE TOWER.

evidence.supports: survey station is the finial on top of the tower
evidence.quote: THIS INTERSECTION STATION IS THE FINIAL ON TOP OF THE TOWER.

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The NGS datasheet (PID DG3603, retrieved 2026-10-21) has the 1941 station description; the Forest Lookouts page reproduces the same text and adds the agency name. The datasheet's history has only the 1941 observation, so there is no later condition report on record. Height from the datasheet is about 125 ft; the record's 38.1 m matches. The Forest Lookouts page gives the USGS quad as Piedmont SE (1967); NGS now lists Piedmont SE (2018); that is a map edition difference and is not used. Two WebSearch calls found nothing else on this tower. A TopoQuest search snippet names an Oak Grove Lookout Tower in Cleburne County; no source ties it to Rattlesnake, and it was not read. Not checked: Talladega National Forest or Alabama Forestry Commission records, and whether the tower still stands.
